_note: Photos and drawings shown on the site. To add one: put the image in src/assets/photos/ (JPEG or PNG, long edge about 2400 px, metadata stripped) and add an entry here. experiments lists experiment slugs, or is empty for project-wide images; kind is photo or drawing (drawings are shown whole, not cropped). Videos live in public/media/video/. Credits and captions marked TBC need checking by the team. Captions in <mark>…</mark> have not been verified by the team or against a paper; remove the tags once checked.

photos.alt: Diagram of BABY 100 mL: helium flows from a cylinder over a 100 mL crucible of ClLiF salt set between two neutron sources, then on to tritium collection and a liquid scintillation counter.
photos.caption: How BABY works: (1) DT generators produce 14 MeV neutrons; (2) neutrons breed tritium from lithium in the salt; (3) the tritium moves through the salt; (4) it is released into the helium sweep gas or permeates the walls; (5) it is collected and counted by liquid scintillation. Used in the BABY guide.
photos.credit: Delaporte-Mathurin et al., Nucl. Fusion 65 026037 (2025), CC BY 4.0

photos.alt: Schematic of a cylindrical tank of FLiBe around a 14 MeV DT neutron source, a close-up of the gas and liquid interface, and a flowchart of the physics involved.
photos.caption: The original four-quadrant LIBRA design: (A) a DT neutron generator surrounded by a cylindrical tank of FLiBe about 1 m across, in four independent quadrants, each with its own sparging and sweep gas system; (B) tritium carried to detection by the cover gas or the liner sweep gas; (C) the coupled physics. Not to scale.
photos.credit: Ferry et al., Fusion Sci. Technol. 79, 13-35 (2023), Fig. 3

photos.alt: Log-log chart of tritons per second against neutrons per second, comparing past breeding experiments, LIBRA phases and planned blankets, with a technology readiness colour scale.
photos.caption: LIBRA compared with other tritium breeding experiments and planned blankets, by neutron source strength and tritium produced. LIBRA dates are as planned when the figure was made and are now out of date (TBC).

photos.alt: Left, a cut-away render of the ARC tokamak with its FLiBe liquid immersion blanket labelled; right, curves of fusion power on the grid over time for three blanket types.
photos.caption: (A) The ARC design, with the DT plasma surrounded by a FLiBe liquid immersion blanket (LIB). (B) Tritium breeding sets the best-case pace of fusion growth: modelled doubling times of 2 years for a liquid immersion blanket, 5 for an advanced blanket and 10 for a conventional one.

photos.alt: Neutronics results: a colour map of tritium production in a FLiBe volume around a point source, and two plots of error and tritium breeding ratio against FLiBe thickness.
photos.caption: LIBRA neutronics: (A) the tritium production rate through the FLiBe around the neutron source, with a 5 cm lead layer; (B, C) how the calculated error and tritium breeding ratio change with FLiBe thickness, with the LIBRA thickness marked.

photos.alt: Plot of relative power density rising as blanket radial thickness falls, with outlines of EU-DEMO, ARIES-RS, ARIES-AT and ARC above.
photos.caption: Thinner blankets allow smaller, denser fusion devices: power density against blanket radial thickness, from EU-DEMO (about 1.5 m) to ARC (about 0.7 m). The figure credits LIBRA-type blankets with better neutron moderation, less non-breeding structure and higher thermal efficiency.

photos.alt: Plot of relative cost of electricity falling and thermal efficiency rising with blanket temperature, with the FLiBe liquid range and the LIBRA temperature range shaded.
photos.caption: Hotter blankets convert heat to electricity more efficiently: relative cost of electricity and thermal efficiency against temperature, with the FLiBe liquid range and the LIBRA temperature range marked.
